Our editorial bar

How we vet listings

Every listing is reviewed by a human (currently Henrik or Vera) within one business day. We reject roughly 14% of submissions on first pass. Here's the rubric:

We require

  • A specific salary range. Bands are fine; "competitive" is not.
  • An explicit location requirement (region, country, or timezone window).
  • A statement of the hiring process — at minimum, the number of stages.
  • A real company contact email at the company's domain.
  • The role to be fully remote. Hybrid postings, even "mostly remote," are rejected.
  • A working application URL or email at submission time.

We reject

  • "Remote-friendly" or "remote in [city]" postings.
  • Postings that hide the salary band behind a recruiter call.
  • Postings that demand unpaid take-home work exceeding 3 hours.
  • Postings with vague or fictional locations ("Anywhere, but we prefer overlap with PT").
  • Listings from staffing agencies posting on behalf of unnamed clients.
  • Listings from companies with a documented pattern of bait-and-switch postings.

FAQ

Employer questions

How long does editorial review take?
One business day, typically half a day. If we need anything from you (clarification, salary band, location specifics) we email the contact address on the listing.
What happens if my listing gets rejected?
You aren't charged until the listing is approved. If we reject, we write back with specifics on what would need to change — usually it's one of: missing salary, vague location, or a hybrid requirement we caught. Resubmissions are common.
Can I edit a listing after it's live?
Yes — edits go live immediately. We do a light second-pass review for any change to salary, location, or hiring process language. If we have concerns, we email you.
Do you take a cut of the salary if I hire?
No. We charge a flat fee for the listing. We are not a recruiter, do not source candidates ourselves, and have no stake in who you hire.
What's the renewal discount for unfilled roles?
30% off if you renew within 14 days of the listing closing. We assume that if the role didn't fill, something needed adjusting — and we'd rather you adjust and re-list than pay full price for the same problem twice.
Do you offer non-profit or open-source pricing?
Yes. 501(c)(3) non-profits and verified open-source projects post free. Email hello@remoteroost.example with proof of status and we'll send a code.
